description: A blue square with a transparent surround, placed at its native 48x48 in the middle of a 96x96 light-grey bed, casting a `shadow` a quarter of its own height down and to the right (12 pixels each way), softness 0.08, opacity 0.8. Expect a soft dark-grey shadow the shape of the square -- not of the picture's whole 48x48 box, since the surround is transparent -- falling down-right of it, its solid part ending exactly where the 48x48 picture does and its soft edge running on past that onto the bed, with the blue square sharp and fully on top. What a wrong render looks like: a shadow that stops in a straight line at the picture's bottom-right edge means the layer was not padded out to the shadow's reach -- the bug a native-size picture exists here to catch; a shadow the size of the whole 48x48 picture means it was cast from the box rather than the alpha; a shadow over the blue means it was drawn over the layer; a shadow up and to the left means the offset's sign is backwards.
